name: MAC address
plain: A page cannot read your device's network hardware address.
meaning: MAC addresses never reach the web platform. Proxies are weak: WebRTC local candidates (mDNS now) and Bluetooth device IDs after a prompt are per-origin and randomized. iOS and Android also randomize Wi-Fi MACs per network.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: WebRTC local ICE candidate
fields.range: formerly local IPv4, now random mDNS name

fields.name: proxy: Web Bluetooth device.id
fields.range: per-origin opaque ID, only after user picks a device

limits.headline: Can't see your device's network hardware address (MAC)
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: See random per site IDs from some features, such as Bluetooth after you approve
See a masked network address from WebRTC
See your IP address on the server side
cannot: See Wi-Fi addresses; iPhone and Android randomize them per network
Link one site to another using a MAC
Get a stable ID from Bluetooth across sites

story.what_it_is: A page cannot read your device's network hardware address.
story.for_you: Your device's hardware address stays hidden from websites. It never leaves your device through the browser. That makes you harder to follow from one network to the next.
story.for_makers: The hardware address is a permanent ID that trackers love. The web never exposed it. Weak stand-ins exist, but they are random or per site.

use_cases.example: An ad network wanted a permanent device ID and falls back on cookies and fingerprints.
A fraud team wanted to block known bad devices and uses a browser profile instead.
An IT portal wanted to allow only company laptops and needs a managed agent.
A router setup page wanted the address of your phone and uses a sign-in on the router instead.
A store wanted to detect in-store visits by phone signals and cannot from a web page.
A game ban system wanted a permanent ID and bans accounts instead.
A measurement vendor wanted to connect two devices and uses logins.

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
